task: Atlas resolver: apply path-derived storefront fallback when an existing Atlas node has no canonical domain ownership.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: After #680 merged, PR #666 plan-only still reports ARCHITECTURE_SCOPE_UNRESOLVED for src/app/oldal/[slug]/page.tsx and src/app/sitemap.ts. classifyAtlasPath now correctly returns DOMAIN-STOREFRONT fallback, but resolveAtlasArchitectureForPath prefers an existing Atlas node even when node.domains is empty, bypassing path-derived fallback. Resolver semantics therefore diverge from classifier semantics.
observableOutcomes: An existing Atlas node with empty domains for an otherwise-unowned public app page resolves through classifyAtlasPath fallback to DOMAIN-STOREFRONT/shared-storefront.
An existing Atlas node with an explicit canonical domain retains that domain and is not replaced by fallback.
Deleted/planned route PO authority semantics remain unchanged and continue to distinguish ownership from deletion authorization/completion.
PR #666 planned projection resolves its live public page and sitemap consumers before product implementation.
unresolvedRisks: Blindly replacing node classification could discard semantic node metadata or explicit domain ownership.
Fallback must only fill missing path-derived ownership, not rewrite explicit node domains.
Tombstone/planned-deletion authority must remain independent from path fallback.

in: Adversarial tests for empty-domain existing nodes and explicit-domain precedence.
out: New authority registry or new gate.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This resolver is foundational pre-execution authority logic. The fix must unify classifier/resolver semantics without weakening explicit authority or deletion proof.

acceptanceCriteria: Given an Atlas node for src/app/oldal/[slug]/page.tsx with domains=[], resolveAtlasArchitectureForPath must report DOMAIN-STOREFRONT/shared-storefront from the canonical path fallback.
Given an Atlas node for src/app/admin/orders/page.tsx with domains=['DOMAIN-ADMIN'], resolver must preserve DOMAIN-ADMIN/admin-operations and must not add DOMAIN-STOREFRONT.
Given a forbidden deleted or planned route, path-derived storefront ownership may resolve while PO deletion authorization and Git completion remain independently governed by their existing evidence.
invariants: Existing non-empty node domains are authoritative over fallback.
Empty node domains may be filled only by classifyAtlasPath path-derived classification.
Resolver does not mutate Atlas nodes or domain registry.
Deletion authorization/completion is not inferred from path domain ownership.

failureModes: Resolver bypasses classifier fallback because node exists.
Resolver conflates path ownership with deletion proof.
edgeCases: Deleted forbidden route with storefront path ownership.

alternatives.summary: Use classifyAtlasPath only when existing node domains are empty; preserve other node metadata.
alternatives.reason: Unifies path ownership semantics with minimal change.

alternatives.summary: Rebuild every Atlas node classification before resolver use.
alternatives.reason: Broader mutation and unnecessary performance/semantic risk.
Product-specific exception would hide foundational resolver divergence.

specialistReviews.finding: Resolver and classifier must share path-derived ownership semantics.
specialistReviews.resolution: Fallback only for empty node domains.

specialistReviews.finding: Node existence must not automatically mean node domain data is complete.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use non-empty node domains when present; otherwise derive from current classifier without mutating node.

specialistReviews.finding: Deletion tests must not regress into ownership-as-proof.
specialistReviews.resolution: Retain independent PO/Git assertions and add node-fallback regression.

specialistReviews.finding: The resolver is called repeatedly by Plan Gate; change should remain deterministic and local.
specialistReviews.resolution: Single classifyAtlasPath call only when node domains are empty.

challenge.scenario: Existing node has domains=[] but public page classifier has storefront fallback.
Existing admin node has explicit DOMAIN-ADMIN.
Deleted forbidden route has empty-domain node.
challenge.finding: Path ownership could be mistaken for deletion completion.
No route object exists, but public metadata still has classifier fallback.
challenge.resolution: Resolver may use classifier domains independently of route presence.

challenge.scenario: Node authorities are stale/empty while node domains are explicit.
challenge.finding: Authority must follow domain registry, not stale node authorities.

challenge.scenario: Classifier returns no domain for an unknown non-app file.
A later exact canonical path is added.
challenge.finding: Fallback should yield to registry automatically.
challenge.resolution: classifyAtlasPath canonical precedence remains source of fallback.

challenge.finding: Both live consumers must resolve before implementation.
challenge.resolution: Use unchanged #666 plan as post-merge proof.

proofPlan: Plan-only Plan Before Code PASS before implementation.
Add resolver regression for existing empty-domain public page/sitemap nodes and explicit-domain precedence.
Run exact-head Edit-Time, Replay, Quality, TypeScript, Build and Truth; CLOSE→LEARN.

requirements.requirement: Resolver uses current path-derived classification when an existing Atlas node has no domains, while preserving explicit node-domain precedence.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Explicit node domain ownership must not be replaced by storefront fallback.

requirements.requirement: Resolver correction typechecks and production-builds on exact implementation head.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No type or production build regression.

notes: Targeted follow-up from #666 after merged #680. Fixes resolver consumption of path-derived fallback; no product scope or parallel quality mechanism.
